steps.title: Scope the parameterizable up/down counter with WRAP/SATURATE modes and terminal-count flag
steps.goal: Write the Overview: an N-bit synchronous up/down counter with parallel load (priority over counting), a compile-time WRAP/SATURATE overflow policy, a tc flag decoded from the registered count and the live up input, and an area-over-speed design goal.

spec_evidence.quote: Fmax is not critical; small area preferred

decisions.topic: Is MODE fixed at elaboration time or selectable at runtime
decisions.choice: Compile-time parameter; only the selected overflow logic is generated
decisions.rationale: The spec says 'parameter MODE', and a parameter also saves area.

done_when: The Overview fits in one paragraph and states the function, the load-over-count priority, both MODE behaviours, the tc purpose and the small-area goal
The Overview states that MODE is fixed at elaboration
The Overview states that count is registered and tc is a combinational decode

steps.title: Define ports and the N/MODE parameters, including how MODE is encoded
steps.goal: Produce the port table (clk, rst, en, up, load, load_val[N-1:0], count[N-1:0], tc) and the parameter table (N default 8; MODE with its legal values and default).

spec_evidence.quote: inputs: en, up (1=count up, 0=count down), load, load_val[N-1:0]

decisions.topic: MODE parameter representation and default value
options: Integer parameter with localparams WRAP=0/SATURATE=1, default WRAP
decisions.choice: String parameter MODE with legal values "WRAP" and "SATURATE", default "WRAP"
decisions.rationale: This matches the spec wording directly and is well supported by Verilog-2001 synthesis tools. WRAP is the conventional counter default.
decisions.question: Should MODE be a string parameter ("WRAP"/"SATURATE") or an integer code, and which mode is the default?

decisions.choice: max = 2^N-1 (all ones); no separate modulus parameter
decisions.rationale: The spec describes an 'N-bit counter' and mentions no modulus, so full range is implied. The user's tc formula uses MAX without defining it otherwise.
decisions.question: Is 'max' always 2^N-1, or do you need a configurable maximum/modulus?

done_when: Each port has a direction, width, active level and one-line description
The tc port is described as a combinational output decoded from the count register and the live up input
The parameter table lists N (default 8, with the minimum legal value stated) and MODE (type, legal values, default)
An illegal MODE value is handled, for example by an elaboration-time error, and the handling is documented
max is defined as {N{1'b1}}

steps.title: Specify tc as a combinational decode of registered count and live up
steps.goal: Define tc = (up && count==MAX) || (!up && count==0), with no flop and no en/load qualification. Document that tc follows a change of up within the same cycle, and that this is consistent with the registered-output rule, which applies to count only.

spec_evidence.quote: tc = 1 when count is at max while counting up, or at 0 while counting down
registered outputs, no combinational path from inputs to count

decisions.topic: tc implementation: decode of registered count plus live up, or a fully registered flop
options: Combinational decode: tc = up ? (count==max) : (count==0), so there is a path from up to tc
Registered tc flop computed from next_count and the current up, so tc lags a change of up by one cycle
decisions.choice: Combinational decode of the count register and the live up input; no extra flop. A registered TC_REG option is out of scope and is only a possible future addition.
decisions.rationale: User answer Q1: tc may be a combinational decode, tc follows a change of up immediately, and only count must be registered.

decisions.topic: Is tc qualified by en (and by load)?
options: tc ignores en: it depends only on count and up
tc = en & boundary condition (cascade-friendly ripple-carry style)
decisions.choice: tc ignores en and load; it depends only on count and up
decisions.rationale: The user's answer to Q1 gives the exact formula tc = (up && count==MAX) || (!up && count==0), which has no en or load term. This agrees with the spec's definition, which uses only count and direction.

done_when: A truth table gives tc for every combination of up, count==0 and count==max
The doc states that tc is a decode and that up is the only input with a combinational path to tc (count comes from the register)
The doc states that tc may glitch when up or count changes, and that a registered TC_REG variant is a possible future addition
The doc states tc behaviour in SATURATE mode while count is held at a boundary (tc stays high while the direction is unchanged)
The doc states that tc is independent of en and load

steps.title: Specify next-state priority: rst > load > en-count > hold
steps.goal: Write the control logic that selects the next count: synchronous reset first, then parallel load, then count up or down when en=1, and otherwise hold.

spec_evidence.quote: inputs: en, up (1=count up, 0=count down), load, load_val[N-1:0]

decisions.rationale: 'Priority over counting' implies load is an independent, higher-priority operation. en gates counting only.
decisions.question: Should load_val be loaded whenever load=1, even if en=0, or only when en=1?

options: rst overrides load and en; count resets to 0
rst overrides; count resets to a parameterized value
decisions.choice: rst has highest priority; count resets to 0
decisions.rationale: This is the industry-standard convention for synchronous reset, and the spec gives no other reset value.
decisions.question: Should rst override load, and should count reset to 0 or to some other value?

done_when: A priority table covers every combination of rst, load, en and up, with the resulting next count
The table states that up is ignored for the next count when en=0 and load=0, while up still affects tc

steps.title: Design an area-minimal ±1 datapath with MODE-dependent boundary handling
steps.goal: Define the next-count datapath: one shared ±1 adder, and one boundary compare (==max / ==0 selected by up) shared between saturation and the tc decode. A next-state mux selects among load_val, the adder result, the held value and 0.

spec_evidence.quote: Fmax is not critical; small area preferred

options: Separate incrementer and decrementer followed by a mux
decisions.choice: A single shared adder adds +1 or -1 (all ones). WRAP uses natural modulo-2^N overflow. SATURATE suppresses the update when the boundary compare for the current direction is true, and that compare is the same signal as tc.
decisions.rationale: The spec prefers small area and Fmax is not critical, so sharing logic is the right tradeoff. Wraparound comes for free from N-bit arithmetic, and the tc decode can double as the saturation detect.
decisions.question: Is a single shared add/subtract-by-one datapath acceptable, given that area matters more than speed?

done_when: Datapath equations are given for both MODE values
The doc shows that WRAP needs no compare for count update, and that SATURATE uses the tc signal as its hold condition
The doc states that MODE selects logic through generate or a constant condition, so the unused path is optimized away

steps.title: Draw the block diagram: count register, ±1 adder, shared boundary detect/tc, next-state mux
steps.goal: Provide a block diagram that connects the S4 control priority to the S5 datapath. It must show that tc is a combinational output of the boundary detect, fed by the count register Q output and the up input.

spec_evidence.quote: registered outputs, no combinational path from inputs to count

done_when: The diagram shows every port, the N-bit count register, the adder, the boundary detect, the priority mux and the tc output
count is driven only by the register Q output
tc is driven by combinational decode logic from the count register and up, with no flop, per D2

steps.title: Document single-cycle timing and the output-path guarantees
steps.goal: State that there is no pipeline: inputs sampled at clock edge k appear on count after edge k. List all combinational paths to outputs, including the same-cycle path from up to tc.

spec_evidence.quote: registered outputs, no combinational path from inputs to count
Fmax is not critical; small area preferred

options: Single-cycle: next count is registered on the next edge
decisions.choice: Single cycle with no pipelining; count comes directly from the register
decisions.rationale: The spec says Fmax is not critical and requires registered outputs.

done_when: A cycle-level waveform covers load, count up, count down, hold and a boundary event in both modes
The waveform shows tc responding in the same cycle to a change of up at a boundary
The critical path is identified: count register through the adder/compare and mux back to the register
Every combinational path to an output is listed: none to count; up->tc and count reg->tc for tc

steps.title: Define clocking and synchronous reset behaviour
steps.goal: Document the single clk domain, the synchronous active-high rst, and the reset value of count. Give the tc value that results after reset, which depends on up because tc is a decode.

options: Single rising-edge clk with synchronous active-high rst, no clock gating
decisions.choice: Single rising-edge clk; synchronous active-high rst; en implemented as a datapath enable, not a clock gate
decisions.rationale: The spec requires a sync active-high reset and a single clock.

done_when: The doc states that rst is sampled on the clk rising edge and resets count to 0, per D5
The doc states that tc has no reset of its own: after reset, count=0 gives tc=1 when up=0 and tc=0 when up=1 (for N>=1)
The doc states that no CDC or clock gating is present

steps.title: Enumerate boundary and priority corner cases across both modes
steps.goal: List the edge behaviours: load at a boundary value, a change of up while at a boundary (tc toggles immediately), en=0 at a boundary (tc is still asserted), simultaneous rst/load/en, N=1, and an illegal MODE.

spec_evidence.quote: tc = 1 when count is at max while counting up, or at 0 while counting down

done_when: Each corner case lists the expected count and tc for both MODE values
The N=1 behaviour is described: max=1 and the two boundaries are adjacent
The doc covers tc asserted while en=0 at a boundary, and tc asserted in the same cycle as a load to a boundary value
Handling of an illegal MODE value at elaboration is described
The doc notes that there are no runtime error conditions

steps.title: Plan verification against a reference model for both MODE values and several N
steps.goal: Define a self-checking testbench with a cycle-accurate reference model in which tc is checked combinationally against the current count and up. Directed tests cover the boundary and priority cases; random tests drive the en/up/load/rst stimulus.

spec_evidence.quote: tc = 1 when count is at max while counting up, or at 0 while counting down

done_when: The test matrix covers MODE in {WRAP, SATURATE} crossed with N in {1, small, 8}
Every S9 corner case has a directed test
Assertions check: count changes only on a clk edge; rst wins; load wins over counting; count holds at a boundary in SATURATE; tc == (up && count==MAX) || (!up && count==0) at all times
Coverage goals include both boundaries in both directions, load during en=0, tc rising and falling, and up toggling while at a boundary

steps.title: Record assumptions and the remaining open load and MODE questions
steps.goal: Collect every remaining defaulted decision (D1, D4, D5, D7, D8) as an assumption with its open question. Record that D2/D3 were resolved by the user and that TC_REG is a possible future extension.

spec_evidence.quote: registered outputs, no combinational path from inputs to count

done_when: Each defaulted decision is listed with its chosen default and the question to ask
D2 and D3 are recorded as resolved by the user's answer, with the exact tc formula
An optional registered TC_REG variant is noted as a future extension, not implemented
D4 (load vs en) and D1 (MODE encoding/default) are flagged as the main remaining open items
